sets.q:
The baker made 13 muffins. The kids ate 8.
Add, subtract or multiply?
sets.why: 8 muffins were eaten. Take away → subtract. 13 − 8 = 5.

sets.q:
There are 4 nests. Every nest has 6 eggs.
Add, subtract or multiply?
Ellie found 9 acorns. Liz found 8 acorns. How many acorns in all?
sets.no: The girls found different amounts. Do they join? Then check your math.

sets.q: There are 9 boats. Every boat has 4 oars. How many oars?
sets.why: 9 equal groups of 4. Double 9 is 18. Double 18 is 36.
sets.no: Every boat has 4. Multiply. Then check your math.

sets.q: Liz has 14 bracelets. Amy has 8. How many more does Liz have?
sets.no: How many more means subtract. Then check your math.

sets.q: Ellie has 4 vases. Each vase has 6 roses. What would you draw?
choices: A vase of 4 roses and a vase of 6 roses
no: Each vase has 6. That is equal groups.

sets.q: 8 kids each hold 3 balloons. How many balloons?
sets.no: Every kid holds 3 balloons. Multiply. Then check your math.

sets.q: Which story needs add?
choices: Liz caught 6 frogs and Amy caught 9 frogs.
There are 4 ponds with 5 ducks on each pond.

sets.q: The farmer had 17 eggs. 8 eggs cracked. How many are left?
sets.no: Some eggs cracked. Subtract. Then check your math.
sets.hint: Check your answer: it + 8 should make 17.

sets.q: There are 8 rows of chairs. Each row has 8 chairs. How many chairs?

Amy plants 6 rows. She puts 5 seeds in each row.
Which words tell you it is equal groups?
sets.why: In each row means every row has the same number: 5.
no: Those words do not tell how many are in each row.
6 rows tells how many groups. Which words say each row is the same?

sets.q: Liz has 7 bags. Each bag has 9 marbles. How many marbles?
sets.no: Each bag has 9. Multiply. Then check your math.

sets.q:
There were 15 frogs on a log. 7 hopped into the pond.
Add, subtract or multiply?
sets.why: 7 frogs left the log. Take away → subtract. 15 − 7 = 8.

sets.q:
Liz has 3 boxes. There are 8 crayons in each box.
Add, subtract or multiply?
sets.why: In each box there are 8. Equal groups → multiply. 3 × 8 = 24.

sets.q: Amy saw 6 robins. Marion saw 8 robins. How many robins in all?
sets.no: The girls saw different amounts. Do they join? Then check your math.

sets.q: There are 7 wagons. Every wagon has 4 wheels. How many wheels?
sets.why: 7 equal groups of 4. Double 7 is 14. Double 14 is 28.
sets.no: Every wagon has 4. Multiply. Then check your math.

sets.q: Ellie scored 12 points. Amy scored 5. How many more points did Ellie score?
sets.no: How many more means subtract. Then check your math.

sets.q: Amy has 5 baskets. Each basket has 8 eggs. What would you draw?
choices: A basket of 5 eggs and a basket of 8 eggs
no: Each basket has 8. That is equal groups.

sets.q: 5 chickens each lay 6 eggs. How many eggs?
sets.no: Every chicken lays 6 eggs. Multiply. Then check your math.

sets.q: Which story needs add?
choices: There are 3 shelves. Every shelf has 8 books.
Marion has 18 beads. Ellie has 10. How many more does Marion have?
no: How many more means compare. That is subtract.

sets.q: There were 14 cookies on a plate. The kids ate 6. How many are left?
sets.no: The kids ate some. Subtract. Then check your math.
sets.hint: Check your answer: it + 6 should make 14.

sets.q: There are 6 pages in Liz's sticker book. Each page has 7 stickers. How many stickers?
no: 13 is 6 + 7. Each page has 7, so multiply.

sets.q:
The bakery sells 4 boxes of donuts. Every box holds 6 donuts.
Which words tell you it is equal groups?
sets.why: Every box holds 6 means each box has the same number.
no: Those words do not tell how many are in each box.
4 boxes tells how many groups. Which words say each box is the same?

sets.q: Marion has 8 boxes. Each box has 9 crayons. How many crayons?
sets.no: Each box has 9. Multiply. Then check your math.
